note: Voice: alloy. PULSE 01 used ballad, which is breathy and intimate — the wrong register for someone deciding at work. alloy is plainer and measurably quicker: 2.28s against ballad-family reads of 2.6–2.9s for the identical line. Numbers are spelled out on purpose: the model reads digits inconsistently, and the verifier compares what it actually said against this script word for word. Nothing built from a participant's own run is in here — counts, remainders, clock readings and their own two words are all rendered on screen and left unspoken, because a voice reading someone their own numbers back turns a mirror into a report.

direction._: calm and warm, but moving. This is someone deciding with incomplete information, not someone meditating: present, a little forward-leaning, no dawdling and no dramatic pauses. The weight comes from what is said, never from slowing down to say it.
direction.enter: practical and quick, a colleague handing something over on their way past. The last line is help, not a rule - no weight on it.
direction.workspace: brief, then out of the way. Nothing here may sound like an instruction about how much to check.
direction.answer: light and conversational, the question asked across a desk with someone waiting for the reply.
direction.reveal: level and unhurried in tone but not slow in pace; straight after a pause, stating what happened and never marking it.
direction.mirror: steady and completely without judgement, and still moving. These two sentences are the point of the whole Pulse - they must land as recognition, never as a verdict, and never as a sermon.
direction.ladder: even and brisk, the same tone for all three, so the escalation comes from the stakes and not from the voice.
direction.end: settled but still moving; a thing being closed, not a conclusion being delivered.

en.enter-1: A teammate is waiting for an answer.
en.enter-2: Can you confirm the current status of Plot A seventeen?
en.enter-3: You have a few places you can check.
en.enter-4: Answer when you think you know enough.
en.answer: So — what do you send back?
en.reveal-1: You didn't have the whole picture.
en.reveal-1-all: The six of them still didn't say the same thing.
en.reveal-2: But you decided you knew enough to answer.
en.mirror-1: Nobody told you when you knew enough.
en.ladder: The same thing you know right now.
en.end-1: You will rarely have the whole picture. And there will almost always be another source you could check.
en.end-2: At some point, you stop. Not because you know everything.
en.end-3: Because you decide you know enough for what happens next.

id.enter-2: Bisa konfirmasi status Plot A tujuh belas sekarang?
id.enter-3: Ada beberapa tempat yang bisa kamu cek.
id.enter-4: Jawab ketika kamu merasa sudah cukup tahu.
id.workspace: Buka apa pun yang kamu perlukan.
id.reveal-1-all: Keenamnya pun tetap tidak mengatakan hal yang sama.
id.reveal-2: Tapi kamu memutuskan sudah cukup tahu untuk menjawab.
id.mirror-1: Tidak ada yang memberi tahu kamu kapan kamu sudah cukup tahu.
id.ladder: Hal yang sama yang kamu tahu sekarang.
id.end-1: Kamu jarang akan punya gambaran utuhnya. Dan hampir selalu ada satu sumber lagi yang bisa dicek.
id.end-2: Pada satu titik, kamu berhenti. Bukan karena kamu tahu segalanya.
id.end-3: Tapi karena kamu memutuskan kamu cukup tahu untuk apa yang terjadi berikutnya.
